summary: Validate whether any business exists and is currently open with up to 99.62% precision. Voygr's Business Validation API is now available on Orthogonal.

Today we're excited to highlight Voygr , a location and POI data validation platform now available on Orthogonal. What is Voygr? Voygr provides a high-fidelity location data layer for analytics, agents, and apps. Their Business Validation API confirms whether a business exists at a given address and whether it's currently open or closed, with up to 99.62% validation precision. Backed by Y Combinator and trusted by partners like Overture Maps, Voygr is built by former Google Maps and Apple Search leadership. How It Works Voygr uses context-aware matching across multiple attributes and multi-source verification. Rather than relying on a single data source, it cross-references web, social, and authoritative data to catch closures, relocations, and rebrands that single-source systems miss. title: United Bank Promotes Zach Carlton to Triangle Market President
summary: RALEIGH, N.C. – United Bank recently promoted Zach Carlton to president of its Triangle Market. In this role, Carlton will lead strategic efforts to drive commercial and retail production and ensure the market's profitability and sustained growth.
body_text: Contact: Sameera Jordan Media Relations Manager Sameera.Jordan@BankWithUnited.com Facebook LinkedIn Email Twitter RALEIGH, N.C. – United Bank recently promoted Zach Carlton to president of its Triangle Market. In this role, Carlton will lead strategic efforts to drive commercial and retail production and ensure the market's profitability and sustained growth. Additionally, Carlton will play a pivotal leadership role in managing public relations in the Raleigh and Durham areas, while representing United Bank in the community through active participation in civic affairs and professional organizations. “Zach has consistently demonstrated the kind of leadership and commitment to his team, customers, and communities that we value at United,” said United Bank Regional President Jerry Ocheltree. “We are confident that the dedication and diligence that he brings to his work, as well as his willingness to take on new challenges, will continue to drive growth in the market and ensure United’s future success.” The Triangle Market includes three United Bank offices across Wake and Durham Counties. As market president, Carlton will continue to work from the Bank’s Raleigh office. Carlton brings 14 years of banking experience to his new role, including six years with United, where he most recently served as senior vice president and commercial lender before becoming market president. He joined United through CresCom as part of the Bank’s 2020 acquisition of its parent company, Carolina Financial Corporation. Prior to CresCom, he held various commercial banking roles at regional banks across the Triangle. “My goal as market president is to establish deeper ties in the region, while also building on the relationships that we’ve cultivated over the past few years,” said Carlton. “I want us to feel like a true community bank, staying involved in the organizations we are passionate about and getting in front of customers in the local community. Raleigh and Durham are both strong growth markets, so expanding our brand in the Triangle is an exciting opportunity for United.” Carlton earned a B.S. in business administration from High Point University and graduated from the North Carolina Bankers Association’s School of Banking. He was also notably one of 30 employees selected for United’s competitive four-year-long Leadership Development Program and was part of the inaugural class of the Bank’s Community Development Lending Program – an in-depth community development educational program for commercial lending employees. A Raleigh native and lifelong North Carolina resident, Carlton is very active in the local community. He currently serves as treasurer of the board for the Project Enlightenment Foundation, which supports early childhood development, and volunteers with the YMCA and Habitat for Humanity. He is also active with White Memorial Presbyterian Church, the Urban Land Institute, and the North Carolina Bankers Association. Zach lives in Raleigh with his wife, Barkley, and their two children. ABOUT UNITED BANK United Bank is a premier community bank and a subsidiary of United Bankshares, Inc. (NASDAQ: UBSI). United has consolidated assets of approximately $34 billion with over 240 offices located across North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, Virginia, West Virginia, Maryland, Ohio, and Pennsylvania, as well as Washington D.C. The Bank is dedicated to growing the relationships it has built since 1839 and offering a competitive suite of banking and lending products, treasury management, wealth management, mortgage services, personal and business credit cards, and more. Learn more about United Bank.

title: 19 Best One-Page Examples & Modern Website Ideas (2026)
summary: Explore 19 one-page examples and modern website ideas, from portfolios to product launches, with tips, tools, and FAQs to build faster and convert better.
body_text: Launching a new website can feel like a huge undertaking. Whether you’re a startup founder, a freelancer, or a creative agency, it always helps to look at successful examples for a little inspiration. Below, we explore 19 different types of websites, from focused one page examples to sprawling ecommerce stores, offering actionable tips and modern website ideas for each. Let’s dive in and find the perfect model for your next project. 1. One Page Website Example A one page website funnels all of your visitor’s attention toward a single goal, like a signup or a purchase, without any extra navigation to cause distraction. This simplicity is its greatest strength. Because everything a user needs is in one place, they are less likely to get lost. In fact, a study found that single page sites can improve ease of navigation, making visitors 60% more likely to return. These sites also tend to load faster, which is critical since 40% of users will abandon a website if it takes more than three seconds to load. Visitors form an opinion about your site within just 50 milliseconds, so a clean one pager with a clear message makes a powerful first impression. Many startups use one page examples for pre launch campaigns because they are quick to build and easy to adjust, making them one of the most effective modern website ideas Best for: Startup landing pages, event registrations, app announcements, and personal portfolios where a single, focused message is key. 2. Portfolio Website Example Think of your portfolio as a dynamic resume combined with a personal gallery. This is your chance to showcase your best work, share testimonials, and tell your story. A personal website is a massive opportunity to stand out, especially since 56% of hiring managers are more impressed by a candidate’s personal site than any other branding tool, yet only 7% of job seekers have one. A great portfolio builds instant credibility by letting your work speak for itself. It’s one of those modern website ideas that pays dividends for creative professionals. Recruiters might only spend a few seconds on a resume, but an interactive online portfolio can hold their attention for much longer. For anyone looking to build a beautiful portfolio without touching code, WeWeb’s templates offer the perfect starting point Best for: Designers, developers, writers, photographers, and any professional who needs to show, not just tell. 3. Creative Agency Website Example For a creative or digital agency, your website is your most important calling card. It must reflect your brand’s personality while showcasing a track record of success. It’s an investment that pays off, considering 75% of people admit to judging a company’s credibility based on its website design. Your site needs to build trust and generate leads. Exploring various modern website ideas can help an agency stand out. Trust comes from displaying expertise through detailed case studies and client testimonials. Leads come from strong calls to action like “Book a Consultation.” Many B2B buyers review around 11 pieces of content before even contacting a vendor, so your site’s content needs to be thorough and persuasive. Agencies can streamline delivery with WeWeb for Agencies . Best for: Marketing agencies, design studios, and public relations firms. 4. Marketing Agency Website Example A marketing agency website shouldn’t just be a digital brochure; it should be a lead generation machine. Structure your site to convert visitors by creating clear service pages for SEO, PPC, and content marketing. Each page should feature compelling case studies and prominent calls to action. This is one of the core principles behind effective modern website ideas for B2B companies. Your website is proof of your marketing skills. A modern, mobile responsive design is non negotiable, as 38% of people will stop engaging if the layout is unattractive. Since most prospects start their research on Google, strong SEO is a must. If your own agency site doesn’t rank well, it sends the wrong message to potential clients. Best for: Digital marketing firms, SEO consultants, and social media agencies. 5. Event Website Example An event website for a conference, webinar, or meetup has two main jobs: inform and convert. The essential elements are the date, time, location, schedule, speaker list, and a big “Register Now” button, ideally connected to a Calendly integration to simplify sign-ups. Using countdown timers to create a sense of urgency can also be incredibly effective, a popular feature in many modern website ideas. Since many people check event details on their phones, a mobile friendly experience is crucial. A staggering 76% of users will abandon a site that isn’t mobile optimized. Your goal is to make it as easy as possible for attendees to find information and sign up. Best for: Conferences, community meetups, webinars, and workshops. 6. Festival Website Example A festival website needs to do more than just provide information; it needs to create an immersive experience. Use rich media like highlight videos and photo galleries to get people excited. For a festival, an unattractive layout can be a deal breaker for 38% of visitors. The site should capture the festival’s unique vibe while being practical. Navigation must be crystal clear, especially for the lineup, schedule, and FAQ sections. These user-centric approaches are key to good modern website ideas. During the event, attendees will rely on your site for real time updates, so a fast, reliable mobile experience is key. Best for: Music festivals, film festivals, and cultural fairs. 7. Wedding Website Example Wedding websites have become the central hub for sharing important details with guests. The focus here is on personalization and convenience. These modern website ideas ensure guests have everything they need. Include a venue map via the Google Maps integration , schedules, dress code information, and registry links. An online RSVP form can also dramatically simplify headcount management. Make the site incredibly easy to use, even for family members who aren’t tech savvy. Use large, readable text and simple navigation. Remember that many guests will pull up the site on their phones for directions on the way to the venue, so a flawless mobile experience is a must. Best for: Weddings, engagement parties, and other large personal events. 8. Real Estate Website Example A real estate website needs to showcase listings beautifully and capture leads effectively. High quality photos and virtual tours are essential, as properties with professional images receive significantly more attention. An intuitive search function that allows users to filter by price, location, and features is also critical. Implementing such features is central to the best modern website ideas in this sector. Today, 97% of home buyers start their search online, making your website your most important marketing tool. A professional, trustworthy design is vital, since 75% of consumers judge a business’s credibility by its site. With a platform like WeWeb, you can connect to different data sources to keep listings updated automatically. Best for: Real estate agencies, property listing portals, and individual realtors. 9. Service Business Website Example For service businesses like plumbers, consultants, or salons, the main goal is to get visitors to make contact. Your website must build trust by displaying licenses, testimonials, and photos of your work. A professional site immediately sets you apart, as nearly 70% of consumers automatically distrust a company with a limited online presence. Local SEO is key, so include your name, address, and phone number on every page. With mobile searches for local services on the rise, a mobile friendly design is absolutely necessary. A user friendly site makes it easy for potential customers to get in touch when they need you most. Best for: Plumbers, electricians, lawyers, dentists, and local shops. 10. Law Firm Website Example For a law firm, credibility is paramount. Your website should project professionalism and trustworthiness. Essential elements include detailed attorney bios, clear practice area descriptions, and case results. Including awards or badges from legal associations can also serve as powerful social proof. Prospective clients will research you online before making a call. Your website is often their first impression, and a polished design, reflecting the best modern website ideas, can be the deciding factor. Since visitors form an opinion in less than a second, you have to get it right. Best for: Law firms, solo attorneys, and other professional services like accounting. 11. Freelance Developer Website Example A freelance developer’s website is a living demonstration of their technical skills. Go beyond a simple resume by showcasing live demos of your projects and linking to your GitHub profile. Highlighting niche skills like “React.js” or “Python AI” can also help you attract the right clients through search. Your site itself is a sample of your work, so it needs to be fast and flawless. A well designed personal website can impress hiring managers more than anything else, and it immediately signals a higher level of professionalism compared to freelancers who only have a LinkedIn profile. Best for: Independent developers, UX specialists, and other tech freelancers. 12. Artist Portfolio Website Example For a visual artist, the website’s design should be clean and minimalist, allowing the artwork to be the star. High resolution images with zoom capabilities are a must, as buyers and gallery owners want to see the details. Providing context for each piece, such as its title, dimensions, and medium, adds depth and engages viewers. The online art market has grown significantly, and a professional website allows you to reach a global audience. Your site functions as your personal 24/7 gallery, building trust with potential collectors through a polished presentation and a clear artist biography. Best for: Painters, photographers, sculptors, and illustrators. 13. Acting Portfolio Website Example An actor’s website acts as their digital headshot and demo reel. Casting directors and agents need to see your look and performance within seconds, so your headshots and video reel should be front and center. A clean, modern design helps your content shine without causing distractions. Your website gives you control over your personal brand. It signals professionalism and ensures that industry contacts find the curated, up to date information you want them to see. Given that casting directors make snap judgments, a high quality, fast loading site is essential. Best for: Actors, models, dancers, and voice actors. 14. Ecommerce Website Example For an online store, the recipe for success is speed, simplicity, and trust. These are foundational modern website ideas for any ecommerce venture. A mere one second delay in page load time can reduce conversions by 7%. You need to optimize every part of the experience, from fast loading product images to a streamlined checkout process. Displaying trust signals like security badges and clear return policies is crucial. The average shopping cart abandonment rate is nearly 70%, often due to a complicated checkout. Offering guest checkout and being transparent about shipping costs can significantly improve your sales. Best for: Any business selling products online, from small boutiques to large brands. 15. Product Launch Website Example When launching a new product, your website should be a high conversion landing page. It needs an attention grabbing headline, a compelling product explainer (often a video), and a single, prominent call to action like “Pre order Now”. Many successful launches use one page examples to keep users focused. The goal is to build hype and validate your idea by capturing emails or pre orders, for example, piping sign-ups straight into a Google Sheets integration . By removing distractions like a main navigation menu, you channel all visitor attention toward the one action you want them to take. Social proof, such as quotes from beta testers, can also be very persuasive. Best for: Kickstarter campaigns, new SaaS tools, app launches, and book releases. 16. Consulting Website Example A consultant’s website must sell expertise and build trust. You can establish authority by sharing your credentials, client case studies, and insightful blog articles. Content marketing is incredibly effective here, as companies that blog generate 67% more leads per month. Potential clients research consultants extensively before reaching out. Your website acts as your digital sales representative, educating visitors and building their confidence in your abilities. By the time they contact you, they should already be convinced that you are the expert they need. Ready to build a site that wins clients? See what’s possible with a powerful visual builder like WeWeb . Best for: Management consultants, IT consultants, and career coaches. 17. Tech Startup Website Example A tech startup’s website needs to communicate its value proposition quickly and clearly to customers, investors, and potential hires. A strong headline, a short explainer video, and a clear call to action are the core components. First impressions are formed in an instant. Your site has to pass the “blink test” and convince visitors your solution is new, better, and worth their time. Simplicity is often the best approach. Many successful startups launch with simple one page examples that focus on a single action, like joining a waitlist. Best for: SaaS startups, mobile apps, and hardware companies. 18. Art Store Website Example An online art store must blend the aesthetic of a gallery with the usability of a great ecommerce site. High quality imagery from multiple angles is non negotiable. You need to provide all the important details, including dimensions, medium, and price, in a clear and accessible way. Because art can be a significant purchase, building trust is key. A secure checkout process, clear return policies, and buyer testimonials can help alleviate any concerns about buying art online. The experience should feel as curated as a gallery but as convenient as any other online shop. Best for: Individual artists selling their work, online galleries, and print on demand art shops. 19. Parody Website Example Parody websites are all about entertainment and shareability. The goal is to engage visitors with humor. The design itself can be part of the joke, perhaps by mimicking a famous brand or using a deliberately retro style. Humor is a primary motivator for sharing content online. A clever, timely parody can go viral overnight. These sites often experience sudden, massive traffic spikes, so using a robust hosting platform is important to avoid a crash right when your joke is landing. Best for: Satire news sites, humorous marketing campaigns, and viral art projects. Frequently Asked Questions What are one page examples? One page examples are websites that present all their information on a single, scrolling page. Instead of using a navigation bar to jump between pages like “About” or “Contact,” users simply scroll down through different sections on the homepage. They are great for focused campaigns and clear storytelling. Are one page websites good for SEO? They can be. While it can be more challenging to rank for a wide variety of keywords with a single page, they can be highly optimized for a specific niche or keyword. Their fast load times and mobile friendly nature are also positive signals for search engines. When should you use a one page website? A one page website is ideal when you have a single, clear objective. They are perfect for event registrations, product launches, portfolios, or any scenario where you want to guide the user through a linear story without distractions. What should a one page website include? A great one page site should have a logical flow. This typically includes a compelling hero section, a clear explanation of the product or service, social proof like testimonials, and a strong call to action at the end (and often repeated throughout). Can I build complex one page examples without code? Yes. With WeWeb AI , you can build sophisticated one page websites with features like animations, forms, and database connections, all without writing code. How are single page examples different from landing pages? The terms are often used interchangeably, but there can be a subtle difference. A landing page is almost always a single page designed for a specific marketing campaign. A one page website can be the business’s entire online presence, just consolidated onto a single page.
